# Locale glossary

This is the canonical source for reviewed locale terminology and style. Each locale below has one hundred and thirty-four reviewed concepts (seven analytics concepts, four configuration/type/shape concepts, four short labels whose form agrees with an implied noun: Dark, Light, All, None, and twelve typography, alignment and theme labels: Fonts, Italic, Weight, Normal, Left, Right, Soft, Primary, Default, Original, Style, Background, and six trash and removal labels: Move "{title}" to trash?, Move to trash, Delete, Restore, Remove, Remove row, and eight sharing and role concepts: Share, Export, Publish, Published, Unpublish, Can comment, Can edit, Owner, and three access-lifetime concepts: Revoke, Never expires, This share link has expired.); plus nine library, selection and ordering concepts, two count concepts ({count} selected, {count} presentations), eighteen search, navigation and preview concepts, sixteen identity and form concepts, eleven progress and error concepts, twelve copy, apply, save, reset and duplicate concepts and twenty-two content field, object name and on/off concepts; these entries do not claim a review of the rest of that locale.

Where a language distinguishes them, three rules split one English label: **position versus alignment** (where something sits, such as the image focus or logo corner, against where content is aligned to), **colour name versus style option** (a colour picker names a colour noun, a button style is an adjective), and **agreement with the row noun** (an option agrees with the noun of the row it sits in, like its siblings). A locale that does not make the distinction keeps one form.

Two rules keep two English labels apart. **Move to trash versus delete permanently**: moving a deck or slide to the trash can be undone, so its label and confirmation use the trash wording and never the word of Delete; only Delete permanently promises irreversibility. **Remove versus delete**, where the language has both words: Remove takes something out of a collection and the thing stays (es Quitar, fr Retirer, sv Ta bort), Delete destroys it (es Eliminar, fr Supprimer, sv Radera).

Search and preview split by role. **Search** is the button that starts a request, **Search query** the field that holds it and **Presentation search** the page that offers it. **Preview** names a rendered surface or mode and is never an action; the two actions are **Preview version** and **Preview email**. **Go to next slide** moves the presentation (the notes remote button and the `onClose=next` option share it), while **Next** is the passive heading above the upcoming slide in the presenter console.

Identity labels split by meaning. **Name** is the name of a thing (an organization, theme, collection or logo) and **Full name** the name of a person, first and last name, where the language distinguishes them (pl Nazwa against Imię i nazwisko). **Leave** ends a membership of an organization; **Leave presentation** only leaves presenting mode for the editor and gives nothing up. **Members** are the people in an organization; **Blocks** are the image cards of the Image cards slide type. Each locale writes its validation messages in one register, named under its table.

Progress and error messages split by action. **Conversion failed.** reports that an uploaded file could not be turned into a presentation; **Could not switch slide type.** reports that the AI review panel could not switch one slide to another type, and takes the verb of that panel's Switching slide type…. **Generating…** means the server produces a result (a report, preview image, alt text or AI slides) and **Creating…** that a new record is made. **Loading…** fetches data, **Uploading…** sends a file to the server and **Sending…** sends a message or request. Where the language has separate words for these actions they stay apart; each locale names its progress form under its table.

Copy, save and reset labels split by action. **Dismiss versus Close**: Dismiss rejects a suggestion, Close only closes a hint, panel or dialog. **Reset versus Discard changes**: Reset sets a timer or results back to zero, Discard changes throws an edit away. **Duplicate versus Copy**: Duplicate makes a new item, Copy puts something on the clipboard. A status message with no noun on screen, such as Copied! or Saved, takes the impersonal form (es ¡Copiado!, it Salvato) and does not agree with a noun the reader cannot see.

Content fields take one word per meaning. **Table versus Grid**: Table is the data as rows and columns (the table slide and the chart data editor next to Raw CSV), Grid is images laid out in a grid (the gallery layout). A field label takes the form of the sibling labels beside it: an image URL field follows the other URL fields (da Billed-URL like Server-URL, es URL de la imagen like URL del servidor), and alt text is the short trade term, as in the source. An adjective that stands for an object agrees with that object (New: it Nuova, pl Nowa, for presentation), and On and Off are full words, never an abbreviation. **Placeholder** is the hint text in an empty field, not a stand-in object (es Texto de ejemplo, not Marcador de posición).

The analytics title names the same feature on the dashboard, in deck settings and in instance administration. The chart description is the accessible name of both views-over-time bar charts, whether rendered with CSS or SVG.

**Relative time has no translation key.** "5 minutes ago", "yesterday" and "now" come from CLDR through `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` in `formatRelativeTime` (`client/lib/format/format-time.js`), in the long style, with dates of a week or older in the UI locale. No locale table carries a word for it, and a translation must not add one: plurals and the word for yesterday are the platform's.

Keys: `common.off`, `editor.slideField.slideLogo.option.none`, `slideType.countdown-slide.field.autoStart.option.off.label`, `slideType.countdown-slide.field.flashOnZero.option.off.label`, `slideType.countdown-slide.field.soundOnZero.option.off.label`, `slideType.kpi-metrics-slide.field.countUp.option.off.label`, `slideType.table-slide.field.animateByCell.option.off.label`, `slideType.table-slide.field.headerRow.option.off.label`, `slideType.team-cards-slide.field.showPhotoFrame.option.off.label`, `slideType.video-slide.field.autoplay.option.off.label`. |

Keys: `common.on`, `slideType.countdown-slide.field.autoStart.option.on.label`, `slideType.countdown-slide.field.flashOnZero.option.on.label`, `slideType.countdown-slide.field.soundOnZero.option.on.label`, `slideType.kpi-metrics-slide.field.countUp.option.on.label`, `slideType.table-slide.field.animateByCell.option.on.label`, `slideType.table-slide.field.headerRow.option.on.label`, `slideType.team-cards-slide.field.showPhotoFrame.option.on.label`, `slideType.video-slide.field.autoplay.option.on.label`.                                                                                               |

Validation messages use the informal imperative without "alsjeblieft": Vul een naam in.

Progress labels are the infinitive with an ellipsis, without "Bezig met": Laden…, Versturen….

### Dutch style

Dutch here borrows English freely; don't over-translate product vocabulary.

| Use                             | Not                     |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| slide, slides                   | dia, dia's              |
| slide-type, slide-bibliotheek   | diatype, diabibliotheek |
| reactie (a comment)             | opmerking               |
| antwoord (a reply to a comment) | reactie                 |
| organization, lead, analytics   | werkruimte, …           |
| detailregel (title slide)       | meta                    |
| kanttekening (the aside inset)  | terzijde                |
| op je telefoon (notes on phone) | notities (QR)           |

The English words for the last three rows are **Detail line**, **Side note** and **On your phone**; every locale names those concepts with one word of its own, never the schema key or the mechanism (D352).

Address the user informally (`je` / `jouw`, never `u`), use infinitives for action labels (Opslaan, Annuleren, Verwijderen), and sentence case for headings; Dutch does not capitalize every word.

Validation messages use the formal "Bitte geben Sie … ein.".

Progress labels are passive with an ellipsis: Wird geladen…, Datei wird gelesen….

Retry requests use the formal "Bitte versuchen Sie es erneut.".

Validation messages use the imperative "Podaj …".

Progress labels are a verbal noun with an ellipsis: Ładowanie…, Wysyłanie….

Niestandardowe agrees with ustawienia (non-masculine-personal plural) in editor.deckSettings.autoAdvance.presetCustom and pozycje (non-masculine-personal plural) in slideType.image-slide.field.zoomSteps.option.custom.label; Niestandardowa agrees with widoczność (feminine singular) in visibility.custom.

Validation messages use European Portuguese "Introduza …" without "Por favor".

Progress labels are a + infinitive with an ellipsis: A carregar…, A enviar….

Personalizado agrees with ajuste (masculine singular) in editor.deckSettings.autoAdvance.presetCustom and percurso (masculine singular) in slideType.image-slide.field.zoomSteps.option.custom.label; Personalizada agrees with visibilidade (feminine singular) in visibility.custom.
